hero.headline: Palm Beach County man arrested after 100 mph chase through Indiantown on State Road 710
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled.

Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly. Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95.

Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest.

Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Applications open for free or reduced-price school meals in Indian River County
cards.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility for free or reduced-price school meals.

Families will need their child's Student ID number, their child's full formal name as listed in FOCUS, a valid email address, and internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Households receiving Florida Medicaid benefits need their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. This is the Medicaid case number, not the Medicaid card number. Families can find their Florida Medicaid case number by logging into their MyACCESS account or looking at their Notice of Eligibility Review letter from the Florida Department of Children and Families. The case number is printed at the top of the letter.

To apply, families must visit www.LINQConnect.com and sign in or create an account. New users can click Register to create a free account. Families should search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their students by entering the Student ID and using their formal name as listed in FOCUS with no nicknames. To start the meal application from the website homepage, families click School Services at the top menu and then select Free and Reduced Meal Application. If using the app, families go to the homepage and click Free & Reduced Meal Application under Quick Links. After filling in household information and income details and submitting the application, families receive an email when the application is processed.

Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.

cards.headline: Martin County residents can get free pool alarms through Safe Kids Treasure Coast program
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County. A pool alarm is one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning, the coalition said.

Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out a survey to determine eligibility. The program is available to Martin County residents with a residential pool, with one alarm per household. The program will continue while supplies last.

A 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm but is not included with the free device, the coalition said. Residents interested in obtaining a pool alarm must complete an eligibility survey available through Safe Kids Treasure Coast.

For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

cards.headline: England faces Argentina in World Cup semifinal Wednesday
cards.teaser: England and Argentina resume one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta, with Spain awaiting the winner in Sunday's final.
cards.body:
England and Argentina meet in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta, with the winner advancing to play Spain in the final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday. The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but intensified with England's 1-0 win in the 1966 quarterfinals when Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced on Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. England went on to win the World Cup for the first and still only time in its history. Twenty years later in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 win in the quarterfinals on the way to becoming world champion for a second time. That game also saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton. England also felt aggrieved in 1998 when David Beckham was sent off for kicking out at Argentina midfielder Diego Simeone before losing the round-of-16 game on penalties. Beckham got his revenge four years later by scoring a penalty in a 1-0 win that contributed to Argentina being eliminated at the group stage.

Neither team has had a smooth ride to the semifinals. Argentina survived scares against Cape Verde and Egypt earlier in the knockout rounds and needed extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in the quarterfinals. England had to rally for wins against Congo and Norway after going a goal down and also endured a physically exhausting game played at altitude while down to 10 men to beat co-host Mexico 3-2 in the round of 16. Lionel Messi has been Argentina's talisman once again, scoring eight goals and providing crucial assists. England has relied on Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham, who both have six goals so far, with Bellingham scoring twice in each of England's last two games.

cards.headline: Everglades Detention Facility 'Alligator Alcatraz' Completely Dismantled One Month After Closure
cards.body:
The controversial Everglades detention facility known as Alligator Alcatraz has been completely dismantled this week, one month after Governor Ron DeSantis announced its closure. Aerial footage provided by WPLG showed the site now sits empty after housing undocumented immigrants for approximately one year.

News of the facility's closure first broke in May. U.S. Representative Maxwell Frost visited Alligator Alcatraz on May 26 and told WPTV he observed clear signs of operations winding down, including packed-up intake areas and a significantly reduced detainee population. The facility had detained roughly 1,500 people at a time during peak operations. Governor DeSantis said 21,000 detainees were deported through the facility during its operational period.

ICE confirmed on June 16 that all detainees had been removed from the facility in preparation for hurricane season. The timing of the complete evacuation allowed the dismantling process to proceed ahead of the peak months of tropical storm activity that typically threaten South Florida.

Environmental groups are preparing to continue their federal lawsuit despite the facility's removal. The organizations argue that both state and federal governments still need to provide a full accounting of what structures were built, what environmental damage occurred to the Everglades ecosystem, and how the site will be restored to its natural condition. The lawsuit seeks to ensure proper remediation of the sensitive wetland area where the temporary detention facility operated.

hero.headline: Okeeheelee All-Stars make history with scoreless run, head to Southeast Regionals
hero.body:
The Okeeheelee Comanches 10U All-Stars have made history with a scoreless run that has never been achieved before in Okeeheelee Park. The team scored 49 runs while allowing zero runs during district play in May. The Comanches then traveled to Auburndale in June to compete against the top 17 teams in the state, going undefeated and scoring 39 runs while shutting out every opponent. This marks the first time in Okeeheelee history that a team has given up zero runs during this span of competition.

The historic achievement came after the team lost tournaments earlier in the summer that they felt they should have won. Head coach Jose Espinosa acknowledged there were close championship and semifinal games where the team felt they were better and should have won but did not. While Espinosa admits he would like to win every game, he focuses on teaching his players something more important. "I don't really coach baseball; I coach life through baseball. For us, it's teaching all those things, accountability and how to work together. For us, it's about making sure that when they do make mistakes, they do know how to respond to that," said Jose Espinosa.

The team arrived in North Carolina this week to represent Florida in the Cal Ripken Southeast Regional Tournament. Player Tate Krass expressed excitement about the historic nature of their scoreless run and the opportunity ahead. "It's super cool because we've let up zero runs this season. It's like the first time it's happened in Okeeheelee history," said Krass. He also noted the unique setting for the tournament, saying, "It's going to be so cool up there; we're playing on the mountain range. There's nothing better you could ask for."

If the Okeeheelee All-Stars succeed in North Carolina, they will advance to the Cal Ripken World Series. Player Jonah Espinosa described the season as one with ups and downs and acknowledged the significance of the opportunity. "It's exciting, you know, it's a very hard thing to do. It takes a lot of hard work that nobody sees behind the scenes," said Jonah Espinosa. Okeeheelee Park has long been home to some of the best baseball teams in Palm Beach County.

cards.headline: Finland House in Lantana celebrates four Panthers players who brought two Stanley Cups
cards.teaser: The Finland Club on Finlandia Boulevard in Lantana has become hockey central for fans of Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov, Anton Lundell, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen.
cards.body:
In Lantana, a Finnish flag waves outside Suomi Talo, which means Finland House in Finnish, located on Finlandia Boulevard. The building serves as headquarters for some of South Florida's most passionate Panthers fans. The Finland Club has been celebrating Finnish culture in Palm Beach County for 80 years. Walls inside are lined with pictures and crests representing every town and city across Finland. Club members gave WPTV Anchor and Panthers 360 host Mike Trim a tour of their gathering place. One longtime member explained that the Finns came with Flagler, building The Breakers, and then shipped back to Lake Worth in the evenings.

The Panthers roster has four Finnish players who have become local heroes: Captain Aleksander Barkov, Anton Lundell, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen. All four played crucial roles in the Panthers' two Stanley Cup championships. Last June, when Barkov and Lundell captured gold for Finland at the World Hockey Championship, the Finland Club called all the Finns Sunday morning and the whole place was packed. Club member Jorma Olsson said the president was afraid they were going to lose the roof when Barkov scored the overtime goal. Last season, 43 Finnish players competed in the NHL. The Panthers hold an annual Finnish Heritage Night at Amerant Bank Arena, where fans have flown from Finland to attend. The Finland House hosts a large festival each year in Bryant Park, typically held in late February or March.

cards.headline: Marlins give viral dog Jonah special day at loanDepot park in Miami
cards.teaser: Jonah, the dog who went viral for staring at another dog eating a hot dog at Bark in the Park, threw out the ceremonial first pitch Sunday with his owner Peter Silveira.
cards.body:
Before the Marlins and Guardians faced off Sunday, the Marlins and Chewy gave Jonah a special pregame experience that included a ceremonial first pitch. Peter Silveira threw the pitch with his dog Jonah, executing what he called a perfect throw over the plate. The moment happened because of a video from Bark in the Park last month that went viral, showing Jonah staring at another dog eating a hot dog. Silveira said he couldn't stop laughing at the video and that all the attention Jonah received is well deserved because he's such a good boy.

Jonah was found in a box at the kill cage in Aruba with his three brothers and was rescued by the organization New Life for Paws. Silveira adopted Jonah a few months ago, giving the dog his forever home with the Silveira family in Miami. At the stadium Sunday, Jonah received toys and love from his Marlins family. Silveira said everyone who commented on the viral video told him their dog would have gone nuts and tried to jump over that seat and eat that hot dog, but Jonah went famous for being a good dog. From being abandoned in Aruba to living in Miami, Jonah now gets hugs, rubs, and love from his new family.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 win over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a play by teenager Lamine Yamal, and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain beat France 2-0 on Tuesday to reach its first World Cup final since 2010.
cards.body:
A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute had put Spain up 2-0. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They face each other on Wednesday in Atlanta. Kylian Mbappé and France, FIFA's top-ranked team, were trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. They instead will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium across the river from New York City.

This win on soccer's biggest stage marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match. Yamal scored in a 2-1 win in the 2024 European Championship semifinals just days before his 17th birthday, and La Roja won 5-4 in Nations League play last year. Oyarzabal's penalty kick in the 22nd minute came after Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge in the penalty area. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament. It was his 30th goal in 60 international games for Spain.

cards.headline: Atlanta police increase security for Wednesday England-Argentina World Cup match
cards.teaser: Atlanta police will deploy additional personnel and resources for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal after videos showed fans clashing in Miami over the weekend.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match.

Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. This is the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals. Argentina has claimed three World Cup titles and has been the tournament's runner-up twice.

cards.headline: Police investigate death of South Africa World Cup player Jayden Adams at 25
cards.teaser: Cape Town police are investigating the death of South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams, whose body was discovered Saturday at a property in Cape Town two weeks after helping his team reach the knockout stage for the first time.
cards.body:
Police said Monday they are investigating the death of South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams, after his body was discovered at a property in the Cape Town neighborhood of Schotsche Kloof at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. The 25-year-old Adams died two weeks after helping South Africa reach the knockout stage of a World Cup for the first time. Authorities have not released a cause of death. Cape Town central police registered an inquest for investigation following the discovery of the body, and circumstances surrounding this incident are under investigation.

Adams' father, Juanito Adams, told South African TV news station eNCA on Sunday that the family were waiting for the results of an autopsy and had not yet made any funeral plans. Juanito Adams said the family is struggling to process the untimely death and that it won't be easy to carry on. Adams played in all three of South Africa's group games as it produced its best performance at the World Cup. He did not feature in the 1-0 loss to Canada in the round of 32 on June 28. South Africa Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said Adams had played in his team's group game against Czech Republic hours after learning that his grandmother had died. There were moments of silence and tributes for Adams at the England vs. Switzerland World Cup quarterfinal games on Saturday.

hero.headline: Neighbors worry proposed 85-acre development near I-95 will change St. Lucie County's rural landscape
hero.teaser: The proposed Indrio Town Center off Indrio Road and Russakis Road would bring 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space to land near Interstate 95, with county commissioners expected to vote on rezoning in August.
hero.body:
The proposed Indrio Town Center off Indrio Road and Russakis Road would bring 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space to the 85-acre site near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace, with county commissioners expected to vote on the rezoning in August. The project has raised concerns from neighbors who worry about how the development will impact the area's rural character.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. The project represents a significant shift for the agricultural land, which would transition to a mixed-use development that includes not only commercial and retail space but also possible residential units.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. The planned design approach aims to manage growth in a more structured way as the county continues to develop.

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. The inclusion of the park and green space appears designed to balance the commercial aspects of the project with recreational amenities for the community. The rezoning request moves the land from its current agricultural designation to planned retail workplace, a change that would allow the mixed-use development to move forward if approved by county commissioners in their upcoming August vote.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
cards.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
cards.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

After filling in household information and income details and submitting the application, families receive an email when the application is processed.

Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at (772) 564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.
